instantiated_cells.justification: §305.031 prescribes criminal penalties (Class A misdemeanor, third-degree felony) for violations; §305.032 imposes a civil penalty for failure to register (up to 3x the compensation/expenditure); and §305.033 imposes civil penalties for late filing ($500, up to $10,000 if more than 30 days late).

Chapter 305 contains no requirement for regular impartial third-party auditing of lobbying disclosure records; §305.034 only directs the Ethics Commission itself to check whether required forms have been filed, which is internal compliance monitoring by the regulator rather than an independent audit requirement.

content.text:
I'll analyze the statute for both cells.

For row_001: The statute clearly defines multiple penalties — §305.031 (criminal penalties, Class A misdemeanor and third-degree felony), §305.032 (civil penalty for failure to register), §305.033 (civil penalty for late filing).

For row_002: I see no provision requiring regular third-party auditing of lobbying disclosure records. §305.034 requires the commission to determine whether registrants filed required forms, but this is a compliance check by the regulating agency itself, not an independent audit. There's no audit requirement at all in the regular sense.
